comments: Same architecture/init as kuralsnet_npu_seg_8x64_kernel3_finetune_dropout.json (0.3757/0.3635, the standing best) but trained on kurals/dataset_process/cfar_detect_and_damp_dataset.py's output instead of plain block max-pooling: CFAR (alpha=5.0, ref_cells=1, guard_cells=1) detects real peaks at native resolution and every non-detected pixel is flattened to a flat background baseline before pooling, eliminating background variance so max-pooling can't inflate it via order statistics. Pre-check (contrast measurement, not yet training) showed this recovers ~19.4x target-vs-background contrast, matching native resolution's own 19.4x, vs plain pooling's ~6.7-7.0x -- at ~89% recall on the pixel used for that measurement. Caveat baked into the dataset: the ~11% of targets this detector misses are erased entirely (flattened to background), not just noisier -- structurally unrecoverable regardless of downstream architecture, a real trade against the contrast win. norm_type=local (not tvt) since cwr_rd_stats_all.json's stats were computed on the undamped magnitude distribution and would be stale here.
